Overview

Thornhill sits just north of Steeles Avenue, the boundary between Toronto and York Region. It isn't a municipality on its own, and it's popular with families who want established neighbourhoods and quick access to Toronto.

Housing & pockets

The historic village area near Yonge and Centre has some of the oldest homes in the region. Much of the rest is detached and semi-detached homes from the 1970s to the 1990s, with newer condos and townhouses along Yonge, Bathurst and Centre Street.

The same on both sides

  • Land transfer tax: Ontario tax only, with no municipal land transfer tax
  • Property tax: Municipal, York Region and school portions. Only the municipal portion depends on the city
  • Pricing: Compare to recent sales on the same side of Yonge

The land transfer tax is the same on both sides. What changes is the municipal tax rate and the rulebook, so always confirm the city for the exact address.

Getting around

  • York Region Transit and Viva rapid transit on Yonge and Highway 7
  • Finch station on Line 1 is a short trip south
  • Highways 407, 404 and 400 nearby

Lifestyle & amenities

Mature trees, ravines and parks, with shopping at Promenade and along Yonge. Community centres and places of worship serve a diverse population.

  • Thornhill Village heritage area
  • Promenade Shopping Centre
  • Pomona Mills Park and the Don River trails
  • Thornhill Community Centre

Buyer, seller, investor

BuyingHow buying works →
  • Confirm Vaughan or Markham for the exact address before comparing prices
  • Older homes may need updates; keep a budget line for them
SellingHow selling works →
  • Buyers moving north from Toronto are a key audience; lead with the commute and the tax savings
  • Updated kitchens and baths stand out among homes of similar age
InvestingHow analysis works →
  • Run the numbers with the actual municipality's tax rate
  • Value a unit on nearby comparable rentals, not a Thornhill average

Before you offer

The questions I ask before any offer here. They're things to confirm, not predictions.

  • Second suites and divided homes. Confirm the unit is registered or legal with the city before counting its rent.
  • Yonge North Subway Extension. Planned, but timing isn't guaranteed. Ask Metrolinx for current timelines and don't build returns on it.
  • Heritage area. Homes in the village heritage area may carry rules that must be disclosed.

School boundaries change and vary street by street. Confirm them with the board (YRDSB, YCDSB) for the exact address.
